Bionic.description:
A part fitted in place of the player's own: a grade of the power cell, the legs or the
feet, the datajack, the eye, or one of stage 1's grades of legs.
Bionic.title: Bionic

Body.description:
Each part of the player's body that can be sold or replaced: still `present`, `sold`, or
the bionic fitted in its place. A whole body has every part present.

stomach.description: Left out while it's still theirs, as in a save from before it could go.

feet.description: Left out while they're still theirs, as in a save from before they could go.

Body.title: Body

Buyer.description: Who trades where the player stands: buys with `sell` and `sell_part`, and fits with `fit`.

place.description: Where: a location id, e.g. "scrap_stall" or "clinic".

name.description: The buyer as the player sees it, e.g. "The scrap trader".

prices.description: What it pays for one of each thing they carry that it buys, by item `id`. Empty when they carry nothing it buys.

parts.description: What it pays for each part of their body it would buy now, by `sell_part`, by `Body` field, e.g. `{"left_kidney": 100}`. The clinic's doctor buys one kidney, never the second. Left out while it would buy none.

fittings.description: The bionics it would fit now, by `fit`, whether or not they can pay, each once. Left out while there are none.

recipes.description: What it pays, once, for each recipe they know that it would buy now, by `sell_recipe`, by the bionic it builds. Left out while it would buy none.

Buyer.title: Buyer

ClockMessage.description: The sim clock, sent after the snapshot, when the speed changes and every sim minute.
ClockMessage.title: ClockMessage

EatMessage.description: The server ignores it if there's nothing to eat, or they can't pay.

item.description: A food item they carry, by its `id`, or null for the meal on offer where they stand, `player_state`'s `meal`.

EatMessage.title: EatMessage

Entity.description: The server always sends `pose` and `facing`. Missing, they're standing, facing south-east.
Entity.title: Entity

EntityMovedMessage.description:
The server always sends `pose` and `facing`. Missing, they're standing, facing south-east.
On a side-view map, someone on stairs or a ladder is `climbing`. Taking stairs, a ladder or a
lift to another map is an `entity_moved` at its end, `climbing` or `riding`, held for the climb
or ride, then one onto the other map, as through a door.
EntityMovedMessage.title: EntityMovedMessage

Face.description:
The way a wall faces. The iso camera sees only south and east faces, and a side-view map
has only south faces, towards the camera.
Face.title: Face

Facing.description:
Which way someone faces on the map, x east and y south, by angle from east through south.
In side view, the three eastward values face right and the westward ones left, `north` shows
their back, looking into the picture, and `south` their front.
Facing.title: Facing

FitMessage.description: Has the buyer where they stand fit a bionic in place of `part`, for its `fittings` price.
FitMessage.title: FitMessage

Fitting.description: A bionic the buyer fits, by `fit`, for its `price` and one of the player's `parts`.

name.description: The bionic as the player sees it, e.g. "Hydraulic legs".

parts.description: The parts of their body it can go in place of, any one of which they give up for it: `["legs"]`, or `["left_eye", "right_eye"]` for an eye.

Fitting.title: Fitting

map.description: The map the interactable is on.

painting.description: Null while the frame is empty.

id.description: What it is, the same for every one of its kind, e.g. "copper_wire" or "lamp". Salvage is priced by it.

name.description: What the player sees, e.g. "Copper wire".

weight.description: In kg, counted against the carry limit.

charge.description: A lamp's battery, from 0 (flat) to 1 (full). It runs down while the lamp is on, and at a plug it charges, on or off. Null for anything else.

on.description: Whether a lamp is switched on, running its battery down. The player switches it, and it goes off by itself when it's flat. Null for anything else.

ItemKind.description: What it's for: `salvage` to sell, `food` to eat, the `lamp` to see by, or a `part` to fit.
ItemKind.title: ItemKind

JournalEntry.description: Something the player learned about the incident: a fact, or a lie told about one.

fact_id.description: The fact it's about. Several entries can be about one fact.

text.description: What they learned, as the journal puts it. A lie is written as it was told.

source.description: Who told them, or the clue they found it in.

flushed.description: Whether the infrared eye saw the resident flush as they told it, which it shows exactly on a lie. Null if the player had no infrared eye then, and for a clue.

leads.description: The leads it opened that are still open: its fact's leads, and none for a lie. Each closes once any entry is about its fact, a lie included.

JournalEntry.title: JournalEntry

JournalMessage.description:
What the player has learned about the incident, in the order they learned it, with the
leads still open. Sent after the snapshot on connect, and whenever an entry is added or a lead
is followed.
JournalMessage.title: JournalMessage

LampMessage.description:
Switches the lamp the player carries on or off. The server ignores it if they carry no
lamp, and for switching on a flat one.
LampMessage.title: LampMessage

Lead.description:
Where the trail goes next: someone to ask or somewhere to look, which turns up a fact. It
closes once the journal has any entry about that fact, a lie included.

fact_id.description: The fact following it turns up.

text.description: For the journal, e.g. "Kofi paints in the lane at night. Ask him what he saw."

Lead.title: Lead

id.description: Unique across the world. Audio for the line carries it.

timestamp.description: When the speaker starts saying it.

duration.description: Estimated seconds to say it aloud.

voiced.description: Whether audio_chunk frames will follow for this line.

flushed.description: Whether the client shows a flush on the speaker: the line is a lie, as code decides it, and the player has the infrared eye. Left out unless true.

MapTile.description: A tile on a given map: the village or an interior, or in side view a street or a floor.
MapTile.title: MapTile

Meal.description: A meal the player can have where they stand, by sending `eat` without an item.

place.description: Where: their home's location id, or a shop's.

name.description: The place as the player sees it: "home", or a shop's name, e.g. "Golden Bowl Noodles".

price.description: What it costs. Nothing at home.

Meal.title: Meal

Mind.description:
What the player knows, which they keep when they collapse, and later when they die. Left
out of `Player` while they know no recipe.

recipes.description: The recipes they know, by the bionic each builds, in the order they learned them.

sold.description: The recipes they've sold to the clinic, in the order they sold them. They still know each, and can't sell it again. Left out while there's none.

Mind.title: Mind

statement.description: The artist on what it's saying.

image.description: The URL of the mural's image, /api/works/<work_id>.png.

MuralsMessage.description: Every mural wall and what's on it. Sent on connect and whenever a mural changes.
MuralsMessage.title: MuralsMessage

source.description: The feed it came from, e.g. "The Atlantic". May be empty.

long_summary.description: Three or four short paragraphs of plain text, separated by blank lines. Left out when there isn't one, so the client shows `summary`.

read.description: Whether the player has read it.

NewsMessage.description: The articles at the news terminals, newest first. The reply to list_news and read_news.
NewsMessage.title: NewsMessage

Notice.description:
A short notice a shopkeeper, the `poster`, puts up at the terminals: an offer, an event or
an invitation. It isn't a work.

text.description: The notice itself, with its line breaks.

Notice.title: Notice

NpcStateMessage.description: Debug state for the overlay. The fields in `state` are up to the modules that send them.
NpcStateMessage.title: NpcStateMessage

statement.description: The artist on what it's saying.

image.description: The URL of the painting's image. Each work has its own.

PaintingsMessage.description: Every frame and the painting in it. Sent on connect and whenever a painting changes.
PaintingsMessage.title: PaintingsMessage

PickUpMessage.description:
Picks up, from the nearest pile within reach of the player, its money and each item that
still fits under their carry limit, in order. Any that don't fit stay in the pile. A nearer
clue is found instead, and so is a clue in the jack they stand at, with the datajack.
PickUpMessage.title: PickUpMessage

Pile.description:
Items, money or both lying `at` a tile in the world for the player to pick up, such as
salvage, a secret's cash, or what they left when they collapsed.

money.description: Cash lying there, which weighs nothing. Left out while there's none.

Pile.title: Pile

Player.description:
The player's state, saved with the world. Each field defaults to the starting player's, so
a save from before the player loads with a whole body, no money, a charged lamp and nothing
known. Their humanity is derived from the bionics fitted and isn't a field, so the client never
sees it.

money.description: In the same units as the residents' money.

items.description: What they carry. Picking things up keeps their weight within `carry_limit`.

carry_limit.description: The most they carry, in kg.

hunger.description: 0 is fed and 1 is starving: they collapse.

left.description: What they left lying in the world, oldest first: what they carried when they collapsed, on the tile they fell on or the ground below it, and anything of a pickup that didn't fit when they took from it. Left out while there's none.

taken.description: When they last took from each pickup in the world, in sim time, by pickup id. Salvage lies there again a while after it was taken, but a secret, cash or a ration, stays taken for good. Left out while there's none.

Player.title: Player

PlayerCollapsedMessage.description:
The player starved and collapsed. They wake at home, at `position`, still hungry, with
their lamp, switched off. Everything else they carried stays where they fell, in
`player_state`'s `left`.
PlayerCollapsedMessage.title: PlayerCollapsedMessage

PlayerMoveMessage.description:
A position without `map` is on the village. Side-view maps have no village, so there the
server ignores it, as it ignores any unknown map.

On a side-view map the position can be mid-air, jumping or falling. The server keeps one in
open air over somewhere to land if it's within the farthest, highest jump the player can make
from somewhere to stand (a run jump with Space held, taking off as late as coyote time
allows), or if it's lower than the last position it kept on that map and within that jump's
reach of it along the row, as in a fall from any height. It ignores a position nobody could
be at.
PlayerMoveMessage.title: PlayerMoveMessage

target.description: The NPC the player is talking to.

PlayerStateMessage.description:
The player's money, what they carry, their body, their hunger and what they know, but never
their humanity, with the recipes they know, the meal on offer and the buyer where they stand,
and what's lying in the world for them to pick up. Sent after the snapshot on connect, and
whenever any of it changes.

recipes.description: Each recipe in `player.mind`, in full and in the same order. Left out while they know none.

meal.description: The meal on offer where they stand: at home, or at a shop that's serving. Left out where there's none.

buyer.description: Who buys where they stand, such as the scrap trader at their stall. Left out where there's none.

piles.description: What's lying in the world for them to pick up, on every map, besides what they left (`player.left`): salvage and secrets. Left out while there's none.

PlayerStateMessage.title: PlayerStateMessage

Pose.description:
What someone is doing where they are. `climbing` is on stairs or a ladder, and `riding` in
a lift.
Pose.title: Pose

Position.description:
Where an entity stands, in tiles: (4, 6) is on tile (4, 6). Fractions are mid-step. On a
side-view map, x runs along the street and y counts rows down from the top, and fractions are
mid-step or mid-climb, or for the player, mid-air in a jump or a fall.

map.description: The map it's on. The server always sends it, and a client that leaves it out means the village.

Position.title: Position

Recipe.description:
How to build a `bionic`, which the clinic needs before it fits one. It's known by the
bionic it builds.

name.description: The bionic as the player sees it, e.g. "Datajack".

parts.description: The items the fitting uses up, how many of each by item `id`, e.g. `{"copper_wire": 3, "usb_c_connector": 1}`.

credits.description: What the fitting costs, from their money.

replaces.description: The parts of their body it can go in place of, any one of which they give up for it, or a lower grade of its line fitted there: the bionic's own, filled in from it when left out.

after.description: What must be fitted first, each of them or a higher grade of its line: a power cell for everything but a cell.

Recipe.title: Recipe

SellMessage.description:
Sells to the buyer where the player stands, `player_state`'s `buyer`, for its price. The
server ignores it if there's no buyer, or they carry nothing it buys.

item.description: One thing they carry, by its `id`, or null for everything they carry that the buyer buys.

SellMessage.title: SellMessage

SellPartMessage.description: Sells a part of their body to the buyer where they stand, at its `buyer.parts` price.
SellPartMessage.title: SellPartMessage

SellRecipeMessage.description:
Sells a recipe they know, by the bionic it builds, to the buyer where they stand, at its
`buyer.recipes` price. They still know it, and can't sell it again.
SellRecipeMessage.title: SellRecipeMessage

SnapshotMessage.description: The whole world, sent on connect. Replaces anything the client had.

map_id.description: The map the player starts on: the village, or a street on side-view maps.

level.description: Which of the generated levels in content/street/levels/ this world plays, picked by its seed: the maps in `levels/<level>/`, such as the sewers.

SnapshotMessage.title: SnapshotMessage

Source.description: Who told the player something, or the clue they found it in.

id.description: The resident's id, or the clue's interactable's.

name.description: As the journal names them, e.g. "Kofi" or "Aris's notes".

Source.title: Source

SourceKind.description:
Where the player learned something: a `resident` told them, or they found a `clue`, such
as Aris's notes or a terminal.
SourceKind.title: SourceKind

map.description: The map it's on, such as a street. Left out on the village.

x.description: (x, y) is the building's tile at the west end of a south face or the north end of an east face: on its south row or east column, whatever storeys the mural spans. The face runs along that tile's south edge (y + 1) or east edge (x + 1). On a side-view map, it's the standing cell at the wall's west end, on the street in front of it.

y.description: (x, y) is the building's tile at the west end of a south face or the north end of an east face: on its south row or east column, whatever storeys the mural spans. The face runs along that tile's south edge (y + 1) or east edge (x + 1). On a side-view map, it's the standing cell at the wall's west end, on the street in front of it.

width.description: In tiles, east from (x, y) for a south face or south for an east face.

bottom.description: The mural's lower edge, in storeys above the ground there.

top.description: The mural's upper edge, in storeys above the ground there.

mural.description: Null while the wall is blank.

npc_id.description: The NPC to send npc_state for, or null to stop.

WorksMessage.description:
Residents' writing at the terminals, newest first, and the notice board. The reply to
list_works and read_work.

notices.description: The notices up on the board, newest first. Apart from the works.

WorksMessage.title: WorksMessage

form.description: What the artist makes, e.g. "short poems about the river".

text.description: The piece itself, with its line breaks.

statement.description: The artist on what it's saying.

read.description: Whether the player has read it.
